label: July 1916
headline: The Dawn Attack
deck: The Somme battle goes on: a night assembly, Fromelles and Pozières
caption: Indian cavalry wait in a cornfield below High Wood
body: Before dawn on 14 July, after a bombardment of only five minutes, British infantry who have crept out into no man's land in the dark rush the German second line on the Bazentin ridge. The attack succeeds where many doubted it could, and in the evening cavalry ride forward towards High Wood.

On 19 July at Fromelles, far to the north, an attack meant to hold German reserves in place costs the newly arrived Australian 5th Division more than five thousand men in one night. Four days later Australians storm Pozières, on the Somme ridge, and hold it under shellfire for weeks.
At Verdun the German army makes its last great attempt on 11 July, against Fort Souville, the final height before the city. It fails, and the Crown Prince's armies go over to the defence.
